items.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: I had a buddy who — Jessie Flurry — who was, like myself, very good with his, you know, carpentry and stuff like that.

ctx.x: So I couldn’t leave. And there was no way I could make enough money in town. So I started my own handyman business with construction. I had a buddy who — Jessie Flurry — who was, like myself, very good with his, you know, carpentry and stuff like that. And this friend of ours owns property in San Francisco, a lot of buildings and stuff. And he always needs — somebody needs a door put on or somebody wants cabinets or somebody wants — there’s a leak in the ceiling because somebody ran the tub over. So that’s what…
